transcript: Last night I saw A Mogo Pop on Broadway, a magic show by illusionist Antonio Diaz. This is obviously not a traditional Broadway show, but that's honestly what intrigued me the most about it. It's only running through next Sunday and the tickets are, in my opinion, egregiously expensive, but I got a rush ticket and $42 for a front receipt was pretty good deal. Show itself was a little self inflating, with numerous biographical clips about Antonio and his love for magic sprinkled throughout, but I was definitely impressed by some of the tricks. Bigger ones like making people disappear and reappear suddenly in different places were fine, but not particularly original, whereas I thought the close up slight of hand magic was a lot more compelling. And it gave Antonio the opportunity to show his personality, and I found him to be very charismatic. Some brief research about him, though, has suggested to me that he's not the most original illusionist out there, and that the stint on Broadway is more of a marketing tactic than anything else. But I had a good time regardless. With that, another playbill for my collection.
